A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KrossFuse/RP-KrossFuse research despite the changed title and broader framing in v2. The methods, equations, results, figures, and appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original clustering, classification, image-text retrieval, few-shot learning, and ablation results in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds backbone comparisons, computational benchmarks, MVSA classification, and diffusion-guidance experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix C.9 adds an inference adaptation that replaces CLIP embeddings inside contextualized Vendi Score Guidance with fused CLIP and DINOv2 representations. The core product-kernel, symmetrization, random-projection, and Fourier-feature constructions remain unchanged. The new unimodal pseudocode documents an existing case; the earlier cross-modal algorithm moves to Appendix A.5.

E1.justification: V2 adds multimodal classification on MVSA-Single and MVSA-Multiple, class-conditional ImageNet generation using DiT-XL/2, and a six-group profession/gender image-text clustering example using SD-XL Turbo outputs. These extend the represented data and task requirements beyond v1's retained classification, clustering, retrieval, and few-shot coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds plain concatenation comparisons across classification and clustering in C.8, MobileCLIP and OpenVision comparison rows in Table 9, and CLIP-based c-VSG as the diffusion comparator in Table 12. COMM is not new: its results in v1's appendix Table 3 are incorporated into v2's main Table 1.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include diffusion assessment using precision, recall, density, and coverage, plus runtime and peak-memory benchmarking with batch size 128 on two RTX 3090 GPUs, including parallel RP-KrossFuse with projection dimension 5000. ImageNet testing also adds backbone configurations. These are additional protocols; the PDFs do not establish changes to the retained experiments' settings.

E4.justification: V2 expands backbone generalization analysis in C.6, adds inference and fusion efficiency profiling in C.7, and investigates when concatenation versus product fusion helps across supervised classification and unsupervised clustering in C.8. Figure 2 adds a complementary image-text clustering case study. The original expert, kernel, projection-dimension, and hyperparameter-C ablations remain.

E5.justification: The new checklist states that results average multiple runs and asserts small observed variance, while explicitly acknowledging absent error bars and significance tests. V1 already reports five-fold cross-validation for text experiments but lacks this general repeated-run disclosure. V2 supplies neither run counts nor seeds, and does not establish that more runs were performed.

E6.justification: Matched earlier benchmark tables retain their numerical values, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 9–12 and C.8. Examples include MVSA-Single accuracy of 74.3% versus concatenation's 71.3%, and diffusion recall of 0.484 versus CLIP-based c-VSG's 0.413. Figure 1 also gains clustering scores. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes its error bound from sqrt(B log(4n/delta)/l) to sqrt(2 B^2 log(2n^2/delta)/l). Appendix A.3 correspondingly revises the Hoeffding exponent and union-bound algebra. This is a localized mathematical revision; the propositions, feature-map constructions, and Theorem 2 remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contribution on combining cross-modal embeddings with unimodal experts while preserving alignment. V2's abstract, introduction, and contribution list broaden this to a general framework for unifying complementary cluster structures and constructing joint kernels for paired multimodal data. Cross-modal/unimodal fusion becomes a key application of that broader claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications about signed kernels, hyperparameter dependence, larger fused dimensions, and dimensional comparability, with PCA suggested when compactness is required. It explicitly confines learned unitary alignment to cross-modal clustering. New discussion also explains where concatenation remains competitive and conditions the parallel-inference argument on sufficient memory.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code access link, explicit projection dimensions in experimental descriptions and table captions, separate profiling hardware and batch-size details, and unimodal-fusion pseudocode. These are incremental reproducibility disclosures; the original encoder choices, C-search range, and general two-RTX-4090 setup remain. Newly specified dimensions do not establish changes to earlier runs.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly attributes the kernel-product/Kronecker identity to established kernel literature and adds a related-work subsection connecting the framework to generative-model evaluation and guidance, including KID and Vendi-based approaches. This substantially broadens research positioning beyond v1's emphasis on representation fusion and cross-modal alignment.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution framing, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 adds a limitations discussion, a related-work subsection, Appendix C.7–C.9, acknowledgments, and a conference checklist. It also moves cross-modal pseudocode to the appendix and foregrounds unimodal fusion, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds the generated image-text comparison in Figure 2, redraws the fusion schematic as Figure 3, and annotates Figure 1 with clustering scores. It brings existing appendix comparisons into the main text, expands Table 9, adds Tables 10–12, and adopts a different conference layout. Most earlier appendix visualizations are retained and reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses two important gaps in v1: comparison against plain concatenation and measured computational evidence for scalability (C.7–C.8). These strengthen the justification for the fusion operation and clarify its practical value. Broader backbone checks and explicit applicability limitations further improve the paper. New application experiments remain sparsely documented and uncertainty is unquantified, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in comparative evidence and transparency.
